title: The Best Marathons and Half Marathons in the Philippines
seo_title: The Best Marathons and Half Marathons in the Philippines
meta_description: The Philippines' marathons and half marathons judged on results from 97,000 finishers: Manila's fast-growing majors, the PUMA and MILO series, and the races worth the trip.
dek: No country in Southeast Asia gives us more results than the Philippines: 45 races and 97,000 finishers. They show which races are growing, where the fast fields are, and which ones leave room for a slower runner.

sections.heading: What the data shows for the Philippines
paragraphs: Our results cover 45 Philippine races and 97,176 finishers, more than any other country in the region [1]. Across 15 marathons (10,789 finishers) the median finish is 5:49, one finisher in ten takes longer than 7:18, and 4.9% break four hours. That is one of the slowest marathon profiles in Southeast Asia, where the regional median is 5:25 [1]. Across 45 half marathons (43,185 finishers) the median is 2:47 and 9.4% break two hours [1].

Women make up a bigger share of the field here than in most of the region. They are 33% of half-marathon finishers, the highest share of any country, and 52% of 10K finishers. In the marathon the share falls to 18.5% [1].

Our calendar lists 122 Philippine races. 120 have a half marathon and 39 have a full marathon, and 78 of them are dated between August and October, the busiest stretch of the year [2]. Of the 51 races that publish fees, the median entry runs from PHP 999 for the shortest race to PHP 1,890 for the longest. The full range is PHP 499 to PHP 4,200 [2]. The full list is at runsea.run/regions/philippines/.

sections.heading: Manila Marathon: the fastest-growing race we track
paragraphs: No race in our archive has grown like the Manila Marathon. It had 431 marathon finishers in October 2024, 2,827 in August 2025 and 5,744 in June 2026. Its half marathon grew from 1,670 to 6,801 to 9,291 finishers over the same three editions [1][3]. It is now the region's third-largest marathon in our data, behind Singapore and Bangkok.

It is also forgiving. The organiser allows 8 hours for the marathon and 4 for the half. The marathon starts at 11.30pm from the SM Mall of Asia complex in Pasay, and 2026 fees ran from PHP 1,600 for the 5 km to PHP 3,400 for the marathon [4]. The results match that: a 5:58 median and one finisher in ten past 7:29 [1]. Its race page is at runsea.run/race/manila-marathon-galaxy-manila-marathon-2027/.

sections.heading: Manila by night, and the races north of the city
paragraphs: The AIA Rock 'n' Roll Running Series Manila is a night race. It starts in Luneta Park and passes the National Museum, Manila City Hall, Fort Santiago, Binondo and the Manila Bay strip on closed roads [5]. Its 2025 edition had 1,275 marathon finishers with a median of 5:37. Its half had 2,471 finishers, 39% of them women [3].

Outside the capital, the Bulacan Marathon in Pulilan was the Philippines' second-largest marathon in our data, with 1,712 finishers and a 5:45 median, plus 1,683 in the half [1]. The Clark area has the most choice. The Singlife One Clark International Marathon had 1,026 marathon finishers with a 5:30 median. The Pampanga Marathon grew from 248 marathon finishers in 2024 to 499 in 2026. New Clark City's smaller field had a 5:58 median [1][3].

sections.heading: The series: PUMA, MILO and the Trilogy
paragraphs: Much of the country's racing comes in series that move from city to city. The PUMA Philippine Half Marathon Series is booming. Its Manila leg grew from 2,371 half-marathon finishers in 2025 to 6,166 in 2026, Clark's from 881 to 1,356, Cagayan de Oro's from 470 to 1,100 and Cebu's from 445 to 1,125 [1][3]. The half medians run from 2:31 in Cagayan de Oro to 2:47 in Manila [1].

The National MILO Marathon, in its 50th-anniversary year, runs 15 races across the country [6]. Its season ends with a National Finals in Clark City, Pampanga, dated 6 December 2026 in our listing [2]. Its regional half marathons are the fastest races in the country. Medians at the legs run from 1:52 to 2:18, and at most legs about half the finishers break two hours [1]. They are not a gentle first half.

The Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia, which builds up through 21 km and 32 km legs, has gone the other way. Its Manila leg fell from 1,760 half-marathon finishers in 2025 to 764 in 2026, and its Davao and Cebu legs shrank too [1][3]. The series finale returns to the SM Mall of Asia complex on 22 November 2026 [7].

sections.heading: Visayas and Mindanao
paragraphs: Mindanao's marathon pick is the Singlife Davao Marathon. It had 568 marathon finishers with a 5:30 median, and 25% of them were women, high for a marathon here [1]. In the Visayas, the Cebu Marathon starts and finishes at SM Seaside City Cebu on 10 January 2027, and the organiser names the Cebu-Cordova Link Expressway as its course highlight [8]. Its race page is at runsea.run/race/cebu-marathon-2027/.

Island races are small, and their fields can swing a lot from year to year. Siquijor's Isla del Fuego Marathon had 414 marathon finishers in 2025 and 201 in 2026. Its half drew 539 runners in 2026, 42% of them women [1][3]. The Siquijor Island Marathon is tiny: its 2026 marathon had five finishers [1]. Puerto Princesa's PalawanPay Trilogy leg had 72 marathon finishers with a 5:03 median, one of the quicker small fields in the country [1].

sections.heading: Which to choose
paragraphs: For a first marathon, choose Manila, with its 8-hour limit and a busy back of the pack. For an atmosphere you won't get elsewhere, try the Rock 'n' Roll night race. For a half with company at every pace, the PUMA series' Manila leg is the biggest. For a women-led field, the Sunnies Run in Makati had 2,811 half-marathon finishers, 47% of them women, and a 10K where women made up two-thirds of finishers [1]. Save the MILO legs for when you are chasing a time.

For how the Philippines compares with its neighbours, see runsea.run/articles/southeast-asia-biggest-flagship-marathons-ranked/. For first-race advice across the region, see runsea.run/articles/best-races-first-marathon-half-marathon-southeast-asia/.

faqs.question: What is the biggest marathon in the Philippines?
faqs.answer: The Manila Marathon, with 5,744 marathon finishers and 9,291 in the half in June 2026. It had 431 marathon finishers in 2024. The Bulacan Marathon (1,712) and the AIA Rock 'n' Roll Manila night race (1,275 in 2025) come next in our data.

faqs.question: How fast are Philippine marathons?
faqs.answer: Slower than the regional average. The median across 15 Philippine marathons in our data is 5:49, against 5:25 for Southeast Asia, and 4.9% of finishers break four hours. The exception is the MILO regional half marathons, where medians run from 1:52 to 2:18.

faqs.question: How much does a race entry cost in the Philippines?
faqs.answer: Of the 51 Philippine races in our calendar that publish fees, the median runs from about PHP 999 for the shortest race to PHP 1,890 for the longest. The Manila Marathon charged PHP 1,600 to PHP 3,400 in 2026.

editorial_notes: Built from Run SEA's results archive (45 Philippine races with full results, plus earlier editions for 24 of them) and race calendar (122 Philippine races), with organisers' published race details checked on 6 Nov 2026. World Athletics label tiers are not given. This is not a sponsored ranking.
